title: Raster images (PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF, JPEG 2000)
summary: Pixel images the tool reads, converts, and writes. There is no diagnostics channel.

items.text: PNG input: non-interlaced, every color type, bit depths 1 to 16, tRNS transparency. Output: 8-bit RGBA.

JPEG input: baseline and progressive, gray and YCbCr, 4:4:4, 4:2:2, and 4:2:0. The EXIF orientation is applied unless --no-auto-orient is given. Output: baseline, no alpha (flattened over the background), quality {{qualityMin}} to {{qualityMax}}, default {{qualityDefault}}.
BMP input: uncompressed 24-bit and 32-bit. Output: 32-bit with alpha.
TIFF input: 8-bit RGB, RGBA, and gray in strips, little- and big-endian, with no compression, PackBits, LZW, or Deflate. Output: uncompressed, with alpha.
GIF input: GIF87a and GIF89a, the first frame only, with transparency and interlacing.
JPEG 2000 input: JP2 files and raw codestreams of Part 1 (.jp2, .j2k, .j2c).
Output format: from the output extension, or --format png, jpeg, jpg, bmp, tiff, or tif.
Adam7-interlaced PNG.
CMYK and arithmetic-coded JPEG.
Palette-based and RLE BMP.
Tiled, palette, CMYK, and YCbCr TIFF, and other bit depths.
Animated GIF: only the first frame is read ('canvasnet info' reports the frame count).
JPEG 2000 Part 2 and High Throughput (HTJ2K) codestreams.
Writing GIF or JPEG 2000: they are input formats only.
Images with a side above {{maxDimension}} pixels: size-limit.
Multiply the size by a factor; --width, --height, and --size resample to a size.
Resampling filter: auto (default), nearest, bilinear, bicubic, lanczos3, or area.
The color transparency is flattened over, for example for a JPEG output.
Do not turn a JPEG upright by its EXIF orientation.
Output format; overrides the output extension.
JPEG quality (default {{qualityDefault}}).
Fail with output-exists instead of replacing an existing output.
The pipeline operations --crop, --resize, --fit, --rotate, --flip, and --pad, and the photo operations, are described by 'canvasnet help render'.
None: the diagnostics[] list of a raster image is always empty and --strict has no effect.
Error code: a valid file that uses a feature the decoder lacks, for example an interlaced PNG.
Error code: a damaged or truncated file.
Error code: the file is not a format the tool reads.
JPEG output is lossy, so decoded pixels differ from the source.
ICC profiles are not applied; an embedded JPEG 2000 profile is reported by the library, not applied.
GIF and JPEG 2000 can be read but not written.
